candidates.source_name: European Commission — Enlargement: North Macedonia country page (annual Country Reports)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual EC Country Report is the single most authoritative external assessment of MK's alignment; Chapter 9 (Financial services), Chapter 4 (Free movement of capital) and Chapter 28 (consumer/financial consumer protection) sections state what MK has transposed, what is missing and the expected next steps, in English, before domestic sources summarise it.
candidates.legal_status: public EU document, reusable under EC reuse policy
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual scheduled fetch of the country-report PDF each Oct/Nov; PDF text extraction and section-slicing on chapter headings ('Chapter 9: Financial services').
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball across report years
queries_used: European Commission North Macedonia report chapter 9 financial services enlargement

candidates.source_name: EC Screening report — North Macedonia, Cluster 3 (Competitiveness and Inclusive Growth, incl. Ch.9 Financial services)
candidates.why_relevant: The screening report is the most granular EU-side statement of MK's acquis gaps per chapter: it records MK's own presentation, the Commission's assessment and the level of preparedness, effectively a to-do list of directives/regulations still to be transposed (CRR/CRD, Solvency II, PSD2, DGS, MiFID II, etc.).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off deep parse of the Cluster 3 (and Cluster 1/4/6) screening PDFs; re-check the enlargement document search for revisions.
queries_used: North Macedonia screening report cluster 3 chapter 9 financial services explanatory bilateral screening 2023

candidates.source_name: EC Enlargement — news / press releases on North Macedonia
candidates.why_relevant: Fastest EU-side signal of regulatory milestones (e.g. the Commission's welcome of MK's inclusion in SEPA, screening completion, Reform Agenda approvals); each item points to the underlying decision document.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly crawl of the news listing filtered on 'North Macedonia'; check for RSS.

candidates.source_name: European Payments Council — North Macedonia SEPA scheme participation (news & insights)
candidates.why_relevant: EPC is the gatekeeper for SEPA scheme geographical scope; its decisions, criteria and legal-opinion requirements define the concrete compliance bar (PSD2/PAD/IFR/SEPA Regulation transposition) MK PSPs must meet, plus the register of which MK institutions have actually joined SCT/SCT Inst.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of EPC news + periodic download of the scheme participant register to track MK PSP entries.
queries_used: North Macedonia PSD2 transposition SEPA accession alignment payment services

candidates.source_name: European Banking Authority — North Macedonia equivalence assessment & opinions
candidates.why_relevant: EBA's equivalence annex for North Macedonia is a directive-by-directive comparison of MK banking supervision against CRR/CRD, i.e. an EU-authored gap analysis of MK prudential regulation; the underlying Commission equivalence decision has direct legal effect for EU banks' exposures to MK.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the equivalence annex PDF once; then monitor EBA publications search for 'North Macedonia' quarterly.

candidates.source_name: EBA Memorandum of Cooperation with South-Eastern European supervisors (Vienna Initiative)
candidates.why_relevant: Sets out the commitment of the MK national bank to align regulatory/supervisory standards with EU ones on an agreed timetable — a durable structural driver of MK rulemaking and a pointer to the Vienna Initiative workstream.

candidates.why_relevant: The ECB/SSM–National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia MoU governs supervisory information exchange over EU banking groups' MK subsidiaries; new or updated MoUs signal deepening integration of MK supervision into the SSM orbit ahead of accession.

negative_findings.description: No public, structured EU- or MK-side tracker was found that maps individual EU financial-services acts (PSD2, CRR/CRD, Solvency II, MiFID II, DGSD, IFR) to their MK transposing act with dates. The information exists but is scattered across the NPAA, screening report and per-law conformity statements.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for a transposition tracker returned only narrative documents, not a machine-readable correspondence table.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any deadline register for MK financial regulation must be assembled by parsing the NPAA and Sobranie conformity statements; no ready-made feed exists to subscribe to.

negative_findings.description: The Macedonian-language query on the EC report and Chapter 9 returned the reports themselves but no MK-language page devoted specifically to Chapter 9 / financial services within the negotiating structure (working group composition, chapter negotiating position).

negative_findings.why_it_matters: The chapter working group and its negotiating position would be the highest-value MK-side document for regulatory deadlines; its absence from search may mean it is unpublished or buried behind mep.gov.mk site navigation.

brief: For North Macedonia, the EU side of the regulatory record is unusually rich and almost entirely English-language: the annual EC Country Report and the Cluster 3 screening report state chapter-by-chapter what remains to be transposed under Chapter 9 (financial services) and Chapter 4 (capital), while the Reform and Growth Facility Reform Agenda attaches money to dated reform steps. Sector-specific EU bodies add depth — EPC for SEPA scheme admission criteria and participant registers, EBA for the CRR/CRD equivalence gap analysis, and ECB Banking Supervision for the SSM–NBRM cooperation MoU. On the MK side the mandatory local-language sources are the NPAA (Национална програма за усвојување на правото на ЕУ) hosted by the Ministry of European Affairs and mirrored by line ministries, and the Sobranie's EU-flagged ('европско знаменце') bill pipeline with its conformity statements; twinning and TAIEX activity (CFCD, MoF, EU Delegation, partner central banks) is the best leading indicator of which directive gets transposed next. The main structural weakness is that no ready-made act-to-act transposition tracker exists — a deadline register has to be assembled by parsing NPAA tables and per-bill conformity statements.
